res.jobSummary: The iPhone Division is seeking an enthusiastic Analog Design Engineer to join a creative and energetic engineering team developing future iPhone products. You will be responsible for the design, implementation, and integration of a variety of analog function blocks and subsystems — including power, audio, battery management, and sensors. This is a great opportunity to be at the focal point of many cross-functional interactions with Apple's internal hardware/software teams, contract manufacturer teams, and IC vendor teams throughout different development stages. We expect familiarity with portable, low-power consumer electronics, preferably in a high-volume, high-quality product environment.
res.description: This role requires strong analog and mixed-signal fundamentals, including a deep understanding of noise, linearity, and signal integrity in mixed-signal systems. You should be well-versed in mixed-signal building blocks such as op-amps, filters, ADCs, DACs, and output drivers, as well as low-power sensor and sensor-interface circuits. Hands-on experience in prototyping, characterization, and debugging of mixed-signal hardware is essential.
res.responsibilities:
Participate in datasheet drafting and reviews for a variety of ICs
Follow through the full IC design cycle: design review, bring-up, bench characterization, and bug tracking
Work with multi-functional teams for function block system integration, including schematic and layout reviews
Support production test, manufacturing, system validation, and troubleshooting
Perform hardware prototyping and demonstration
res.preferredQualifications:
Experience across multiple analog domains: power management, audio analog circuits, sensor interfaces, or battery management
Exposure to IC definition, IP development, and cross-functional collaboration with software, mechanical, and thermal teams
MS or PhD in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
res.minimumQualifications:
BS/MS in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
2+ years of industry experience
Strong analog/mixed-signal fundamentals: noise, linearity, signal integrity in mixed-signal systems
Deep understanding of mixed-signal building blocks: op-amps, filters, ADCs/DACs, output drivers
Familiarity with low-power electronics, sensors, and sensor-interface circuits
Hands-on experience with prototyping, characterization, and debugging of mixed-signal hardware
Excellent interpersonal skills with strong verbal and written communication

en_US.name: Pay & Benefits
en_US.content:
At Apple, base pay is one part of our total compensation package and is determined within a range. This provides the opportunity to progress as you grow and develop within a role. The base pay range for this role is between $150,400 and $225,300, and your base pay will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, and location.

Apple employees also have the opportunity to become an Apple shareholder through participation in Apple’s discretionary employee stock programs. Apple employees are eligible for discretionary restricted stock unit awards, and can purchase Apple stock at a discount if voluntarily participating in Apple’s Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You’ll also receive benefits including: Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits, a range of discounted products and free services, and for formal education related to advancing your career at Apple, reimbursement for certain educational expenses — including tuition. Additionally, this role might be eligible for discretionary bonuses or commission payments as well as relocation. Learn more about Apple Benefits

Note: Apple benefit, compensation and employee stock programs are subject to eligibility requirements and other terms of the applicable plan or program.
